name: nonApi_updateRunCountsByUser
description: Recalculates all run-count statistics for a single hasher across all kennels in five stages: (1) insert HasherKennelMap rows for any kennel the user has attended without one; (2) recompute the six HasherEventMap count columns with window functions over the user's QUALIFYING runs — AttendenceState >= 20, VirginVisitorType 0, event counted, visible, not removed, and EventStartDateTimeGmt earlier than 6 h from now (a pre-start check-in tallies in real time; a far-future check-in does not); (3) NULL the counts on rows that no longer qualify (not only AttendenceState < 20 — also virgin/visitor, missing/uncounted/hidden/removed event, start more than 6 h away), or Stage 4's MAX() would over-count from stale values; (4) recompute the HasherKennelMap summary counters (HcTotalRunCount, HcHaringCount, YtdTotalRunCount, YtdHaringCount, DateOfLastRun; CurrentHaringCount / CurrentPackRunCount / HistoricalPackRunCount forced to 0); (5) recompute RollingYearTotalRunCount / RollingYearHaringCount as the runs in the LAST 365 DAYS counted back from today (since 2026-09: the earlier 182-day bucket anchored six months in the past dropped the newest runs), driven from HKM with a LEFT JOIN so a count can be cleared as well as corrected. Every stage writes only rows whose values change, and the haring guards compare the CASE-adjusted value actually written (2026-07-30 fix). No-op for an anonymous or unknown hasher. Called (EXEC) inside and after transactions by portal and app SPs; internal, no auth. Returns nothing. No TRY/CATCH: an error propagates to the caller's CATCH.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Internal hasher UUID to recalculate. SP is a no-op if the hasher does not exist or has isAnonymous = 1.

sideEffects: Stage 1: May INSERT HC.HasherKennelMap rows (all counters 0, permissions 0, DiscountDescription '') for kennels the user attended without an HKM row.

Stage 2: UPDATEs HC.HasherEventMap TotalRuns, TotalHaring, TotalRunsThisKennel, TotalHaringThisKennel, YtdTotalRunsThisKennel, YtdHaringThisKennel, updatedAt for the user's qualifying rows whose values changed.
Stage 3: NULLs the same six columns (and stamps updatedAt) on the user's rows that no longer qualify and still hold a value.

Stage 4: UPDATEs HC.HasherKennelMap HcTotalRunCount, HcHaringCount, YtdTotalRunCount, YtdHaringCount, DateOfLastRun, zeroes CurrentHaringCount / CurrentPackRunCount / HistoricalPackRunCount, stamps updatedAt — where any value changed.
Stage 5: UPDATEs HC.HasherKennelMap RollingYearTotalRunCount, RollingYearHaringCount, updatedAt where changed — every HKM row of the user, so a count with no qualifying runs left goes to 0.

codeSmells.issue: Stage 3 scans every HEM row of the user, not just the affected ones
codeSmells.detail: The Stage 3 UPDATE (lines 164–191) is scoped to @userId only — it re-evaluates qualification for every row the user has, and the LEFT JOIN to HC.Event is per row. Correct, and the second predicate (some count IS NOT NULL) limits the writes, but a user with a long RSVP-only or visitor history pays the full scan on every RSVP/check-in. No practical impact for typical users.

codeSmells.issue: Stage 4 unconditionally zeros CurrentHaringCount, CurrentPackRunCount, HistoricalPackRunCount
codeSmells.detail: These three columns are set to 0 in every HKM UPDATE regardless of their current value. CurrentHaringCount and CurrentPackRunCount appear to be deprecated columns (no logic computes their correct value here). Zeroing them on every run-count recalculation is correct for the current data model but may be surprising to any code that expects them to hold meaningful values.

The SP has SET XACT_ABORT ON but no TRY/CATCH. Errors in any stage propagate as raw exceptions to the caller. Since this SP is typically called inside a caller's transaction, XACT_ABORT ensures the caller's transaction is rolled back, but there is no structured error rowset.

@userId has no SQL default. Called only by EXEC from the attendance and payment SPs, which always pass it. A call that omits one fails before the body runs — no HC.ErrorLog row, no graceful check (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default').

codeSmells.issue: Unused INNER JOINs to HC.Kennel, HC.City and DomainValues.Timezone act as a filter
codeSmells.detail: Stages 2 and 5 (lines 124–126, 279–281) join Kennel → City → Timezone but never read tz (the time gate uses EventStartDateTimeGmt directly). The joins only drop runs of a kennel whose city has no timezone row. Same shape in nonApi_updateRunCountsForAllUsers and nonApi_updateRunCountsForEventUsers (inherited from HC5.fn_GetRunCounts); change all three together if it is ever removed.

codeSmells.issue: GETDATE() (server local) decides 'this year' and the 365-day bucket
codeSmells.detail: Lines 196 and 266–275 use GETDATE() where the rest of the stages use SYSUTCDATETIME(); EventStartLocal is a wall clock, so a local-ish 'today' is arguably right, but it is the server's zone (UTC on Azure SQL), not the kennel's. A run late on 31 December can count as last year for a kennel east of UTC. Same in both siblings.

breakingChanges: @eventDateTime parameter removed (was accepted in HC5 but never used in the SP body).
Timezone-aware event filter added to Stage 2 HEM update (was absent in HC5 nonApi_updateRunCountsByUser; HC5.fn_GetRunCounts already applied this filter).
HC4.vwRunCountsRolling (no timezone filter) replaced with the timezone-aware logic inlined from HC5.fn_GetRunCountsRolling.
Asymmetric COALESCE sentinels (-999/999) in change-detection comparisons replaced with ISNULL(x, -1) pattern.

2026-09: Stage 5 bucket changed from DATEDIFF(day, DATEADD(month, -6, today), EventStartLocal) / 182 to DATEDIFF(day, EventStartLocal, today) / 365, and the UPDATE now drives from HKM with a LEFT JOIN so a rolling count can be cleared. RollingYear* now means the last 365 days.
